sum: The old approach to Everest on foot: from Jiri over the Lamjura La and through Junbesi and Kharikhola to join the main trail near Lukla, then on to base camp and Kala Patthar.

guide.note: The Nepal Tourism Board has required foreign trekkers to hire a licensed guide since April 2023, and that covers the Gaurishankar and Solu part of this route. Checks on the trail are inconsistent, and Khumbu itself has not enforced the rule. On the walk-in a guide helps most where new jeep tracks have cut the old trail: the foot short-cuts are unsigned, and the right one is often not the obvious one.

access: Buses for Jiri leave the old bus park at Ratna Park in Kathmandu early each morning and take seven to eight hours by way of Charikot. Several carry on to Shivalaya, and in the dry months jeeps go as far as Bhandar. You finish with the flight out of Lukla, which depends on the weather, so keep a spare day at the end.

photo.a: A dirt footpath curves across a grassy hillside dotted with pines, with the houses and fields of Junbesi in the forested valley below.
photo.c: The trail down to Junbesi in Solu

includes: porter in most packages (the cheapest tiers leave one out)
Gaurishankar, Sagarmatha park and Khumbu municipality permits
lodge beds and three meals a day on the trek
bus or jeep to the start and the Lukla flight back (confirm the flight is in the price)
airport transfers; Kathmandu hotel nights in some packages

permits.name: Gaurishankar Conservation Area Permit
permits.where: Online at NTNC's e-permit site or at the Tourist Service Centre in Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu. A permit issued at a trail checkpost costs double.

permits.name: Sagarmatha National Park entry permit
permits.where: At the park gate in Monjo, or in advance at the park counter in the Tourist Service Centre, Bhrikutimandap, Kathmandu.

permits.name: Khumbu Pasang Lhamu Rural Municipality entry permit
permits.where: At the municipality's tourist information centre in Lukla when you land, or at the Monjo checkpoint if you walk in from the road. It cannot be bought in Kathmandu.

transportText: Bus from Kathmandu to Jiri, and one flight out of Lukla at the end
tips: Bring all your cash from Kathmandu. Jiri has banks, but there is no dependable cash machine between there and Namche.
Lodges in Solu are family homes with a few rooms, cheaper and quieter than in Khumbu. Out of season some close, so ask each morning what is open ahead.
Between the Taksindu La and the Dudh Koshi you lose almost 1,600 m. Use two poles and take the descent slowly.
The Gaurishankar permit can be bought in Kathmandu or at the Shivalaya checkpost. The national park and Khumbu municipality permits are both issued at Monjo.
Start walking by seven. Mornings are clear and cool; by early afternoon the low valleys are hot and the passes are in cloud.

days.note: The road leaves the Araniko Highway at the Sun Koshi, climbs over a ridge above 2,500 m, passes Charikot and drops to the Tamakoshi before the last climb to Jiri. Sleep here, or stay on the bus for another hour or two to Shivalaya and start from there.

The classic first stage. Climb about 500 m over a forested ridge and drop past the hamlet of Mali to the Khimti Khola at Shivalaya. Buses now cover this stretch by road, and many trekkers ride it and begin walking tomorrow.

Show or buy your Gaurishankar permit at the checkpost, then climb 900 m with little respite to the mani walls at Deurali. Bhandar lies 500 m below on the far side, down through fields. It is the first hard day; start early and climb in the shade.

Lose 600 m through terraces and forest to the Likhu Khola, cross the suspension bridge and follow the river up to Kinja for lunch. The afternoon is a steep, hot climb of 950 m up the ridge to Sete. A jeep track runs through the first half; the footpath cuts across it.

days.t: Sete to Junbesi over the Lamjura La
days.note: Climb another 950 m through Dagchu and Goyam, in rhododendron and moss forest, to the Lamjura La, the highest point before Namche. Descend through fir forest to Taktor and round the hillside into Junbesi. Carry a warm layer; the pass is often in cloud by noon.

days.t: Junbesi to Nunthala over the Taksindu La
days.note: Climb round the ridge to Phurteng, where Everest shows for the first time on a clear morning, drop to the Ringmo Khola and climb through the apple orchards of Ringmo to the stupa on the Taksindu La. A long, stony descent past the monastery ends at Nunthala.

Down for two hours to the bridge over the Dudh Koshi at about 1,500 m, the lowest point of the walk-in, then up through the Rai village of Jubing and over a spur to Kharikhola. A last steep climb of 400 m from the stream below leads to Bupsa. It is hot at midday; start early.

Climb through forest to the Kari La shoulder, which maps put anywhere between 2,850 and 3,100 m, contour round a deep side valley to Paiya and cross the Chutok La before a steep drop to Surke. Mule trains supplying Khumbu use this stretch, so the trail is churned and muddy after rain.

Lukla's airstrip is directly above, but the walking route stays below it: climb through Chaurikharka to Chheplung, where you meet the main trail and, all at once, a great many other trekkers. An easy stretch beside the river leads on to Phakding.

Buy the national park and Khumbu municipality permits at Monjo, cross the high bridge and climb 600 m to Namche. After nine days on the trail the hill is easier for you than for people who flew in yesterday, but the altitude is new for everyone.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: You are fit by now, but fitness is not acclimatization: nothing so far has been above 3,530 m. Walk up to the Everest View Hotel ridge, loop through Khumjung and sleep a second night in Namche like everyone else.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: The balcony trail to Kyangjuma, the drop to the river at Phunki Tenga and the 600 m climb to the monastery. After Solu the path feels like a highway and the lodges like hotels.

Through Deboche and across the Imja Khola to Pangboche, then above the last trees into the wide upper valley. You sleep at 4,410 m, almost 900 m higher than any point on the walk-in, so arrive slowly and rest.
Climb the ridge behind the village toward Nangkartshang for as long as it feels comfortable, then come down for lunch. This rest day matters as much for you as for anyone who flew in.

A broad terrace to Thukla, the steep moraine above it with its rows of memorials to climbers, then a level stretch beside the glacier to Lobuche. Expect a poor night's sleep at 4,940 m; almost everyone has one.

days.t: Lobuche to Gorak Shep and Everest Base Camp
days.note: Reach Gorak Shep by late morning, leave your pack and go on across the rubble of the Khumbu Glacier to base camp, the end of the trail you began in Jiri. Turn back by early afternoon whatever point you have reached.

days.t: Kala Patthar, then down to Pheriche
days.note: A cold climb to Kala Patthar before sunrise for the view of Everest that base camp does not give, breakfast at Gorak Shep, then a long descent past Lobuche and Thukla to Pheriche.
Down through Pangboche and Tengboche to Namche, with the climbs to the monastery and from the river still to do. A long day, though by now your legs are well up to it.
med: Um Hong Gil Namche Community Hospital

days.note: Down the Namche hill and along the valley to Chheplung, where the trail you came in on branches off below. Carry on up to Lukla and reconfirm your flight at the airline office.
Most people fly out, to Kathmandu or to Manthali. If flights are grounded you already know the alternative: two days' walk back down to the road at Thamdanda or Kharikhola and a jeep from there.
